criteria.label: Utility
criteria.question: Is there a real user, a real problem and a decision I can follow?

criteria.label: Tests
criteria.question: Do tests pass, including the failure case, from the frozen commit?

criteria.label: Devnet evidence
criteria.question: Can I open a transaction or address and see what the slide says?

checks.text: Names a user and a problem in one sentence
checks.evidence: first slide and first 30 seconds

checks.text: Runs from a clean checkout using only the README
checks.evidence: a fresh clone, the README commands

checks.text: Shows one decision end to end: input, rule, result
checks.evidence: the live proof part

checks.text: States what it does not do
checks.evidence: limitations in the README and said aloud

checks.text: npm test passes and the report is attached
checks.evidence: test report file in the demo pack

checks.text: A test covers the failure case (a bad input is refused)
checks.evidence: a named test for the bad input

checks.text: Tests run offline on recorded data
checks.evidence: run with Wi-Fi off

checks.text: The test report is from the frozen commit
checks.evidence: commit hash in the report matches the pack

checks.text: Shows a devnet address, or says there is none and why
checks.evidence: address on the slide or a stated reason

checks.text: At least one devnet transaction link opens
checks.evidence: explorer link with cluster=devnet

checks.text: What the slide claims matches what the link shows
checks.evidence: the transaction shows the claimed action

checks.text: Reads labelled public mainnet; writes labelled devnet only
checks.evidence: labels on the slide and in the README

pack.name: risk-hooked agent (sample)
